1.explanation: This script pulls in the same TableFormatter and Handlebars setup that Lighthouse uses. We register the helpers, define a single row whose “code” field starts with a backtick and contains underscores and Markdown link syntax, then render both the HTML and the plain-text (‘pretty’) outputs. You’ll see `<em>` tags around parts of the snippet (from the underscores) and `<a>` tags around the link syntax, demonstrating the bug—the snippet should stay verbatim since it begins with a backtick but instead is still being run through Markdown processing.
1.bug_scenario: The table formatter is wrapping code snippets in backticks and code fences, but it’s still running them through a Markdown-to-HTML (or Markdown-to-text) pass. Any underscores (`_`) inside the snippet become `` tags and any bracketed link syntax (`[text](url)`) becomes `` tags. In the provided screenshots you can see `` elements around zeroes (`0`) and `` tags around your “t” link, all coming from the formatter mis-parsing your snippet as Markdown.
